commands.review_summary:
This PR changes the xurl skill's npm installer metadata from `id`/`kind` `npm` to `id`/`kind` `node`.

Reproducibility: Partly: source inspection shows current main uses `kind: "npm"` even though OpenClaw only supports `node` for npm-backed package installs. I did not run a live OpenClaw installer path.
commands.review_followup: - [P1] Contributor follow-up is needed for the install-id compatibility fix and after-fix real behavior proof; ClawSweeper should not repair an external PR while proof is missing.

target.title: fix(xurl): use install kind "node" instead of invalid "npm"
target.body:
Trivial fix that skillsaw caught. It triggered the
[openclaw-metadata](https://skillsaw.org/rules/openclaw-metadata/) rule:

> ⚠ WARNING (openclaw-metadata) [skills/xurl/SKILL.md:21]:
> 'metadata.openclaw.install[1].kind' is 'npm', expected one of:
> ['brew', 'download', 'go', 'node', 'uv']

`npm` isn't a valid install `kind` — it's a value of the
`skills.install.nodeManager` setting (`npm`/`pnpm`/`yarn`/`bun`), which the
`node` kind honors. So npm-based installs should use `kind: "node"` with a
`package` field, which is what this changes.

As far as I can tell it also matters functionally: openclaw's installer
switches on `spec.kind` with cases for `brew`/`node`/`go`/`uv`/`download`
and a `default` of `"unsupported installer"`, so the `npm` entry looks like
it would have been skipped rather than installing anything. With
`kind: "node"` it runs `npm install -g @xdevplatform/xurl`.

```diff
             {
-              "id": "npm",
-              "kind": "npm",
+              "id": "node",
+              "kind": "node",
               "package": "@xdevplatform/xurl",
               "bins": ["xurl"],
               "label": "Install xurl (npm)",
             },
```

The `package` and `bins` fields were already correct for the `node` kind;
only `kind` (and the entry `id`) changed. Please double-check against the
runtime if you have it handy.

Refs: https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools/skills
